title: Comparison of the supported affine-origin class with the projective Chern generator
statement:
Let $\Omega$ be an algebraically closed field, $N\geq1$ invertible in $\Omega$, and $A$ a finite commutative ring with $NA=0$. Put $S=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, $P=\mathbf P^1_S$ with coordinates $[x_0:x_1]$, $X=D(x_0)=\mathbf A^1_S$, $t=x_1/x_0$, $j:X\hookrightarrow P$, and let $i_0:S\hookrightarrow X$ and $\bar i_0=ji_0:S\hookrightarrow P$ be the origin $t=0$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change, def-sbc-affine-space]. Work in ordinary small etale derived categories of constant $A$-modules [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], with $L_T=\mu^{\mathrm{et}}_{N,T}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/N}A_T$ [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback] and ordinary compact supports [def-amb-etale-compact-support]. Write $c_{0,X}:i_{0*}A\to L_X[2]$ and $c_{0,P}:\bar i_{0*}A\to L_P[2]$ for the relative supported Kummer divisor morphisms of [lem-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer]. They use the divisor line bundles and their canonical sections off the origin, with the boundary convention of [def-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer-boundary].

Let $\epsilon_M:j_!j^{-1}M\to M$ denote the extension-by-zero counit and let $e=\epsilon_{\bar i_{0*}A}:j_!i_{0*}A\to\bar i_{0*}A$, using $j^{-1}\bar i_{0*}A=i_{0*}A$. Then $e$ is an isomorphism and the actual morphisms satisfy
$$\epsilon_{L_P[2]}\circ j_!c_{0,X}=c_{0,P}\circ e.$$
For $D_0=\bar i_0(S)$, the divisor line bundle $\mathcal O_P(D_0)$ of [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle] is $\mathcal O_P(1)$ with transition $g_0=t^{-1}g_1$ on the standard charts. Let $h:A\to R\Gamma(P,L_P[2])$ be its ordinary Kummer first Chern class. Let $\tau_X^e:A\to C=R\Gamma_c(X,L_X[2])$ be the compact image of $c_{0,X}$, using $R\Gamma_c(X,i_{0*}A)=A$, and let $a:C\to R\Gamma(P,L_P[2])$ be induced by $\epsilon_{L_P[2]}$. Then
$$a\circ\tau_X^e=h.$$
In particular this is the positive Chern class itself, with coefficient $+1$, rather than an unspecified multiple of it. No identification of supported cohomology with compact cohomology is assumed.

proof.text: Put $U_0=D(x_0)=X$ and $U_1=D(x_1)=P-D_0$. The ideal of $D_0$ has frames $f_0=t$ on $U_0$ and $f_1=1$ on $U_1$. These generate Cartier ideals: $t$ is a non-zero-divisor in $\Omega[t]$, and $1$ is a non-zero-divisor on $U_1$. For the dual ideal [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle], the dual frames satisfy $g_0=t^{-1}g_1$ on the overlap. The frame identifications $g_a\mapsto e_a^{(1)}$ therefore glue to an isomorphism $\mathcal O_P(D_0)\cong\mathcal O_P(1)$ by the transition rule of [def-pc-projective-space-twist]. The canonical divisor section has coordinates $t$ and $1$ in these frames, respectively; it is thus the section $x_1$ of the positive twist. Restriction to $X$ gives precisely the divisor pair used to define $c_{0,X}$.

proof.text: Write $F=\bar i_{0*}A_S$ and $G=i_{0*}A_S$. Open inverse image is restriction, as specified in [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction]. Thus on every etale $V\to X$ the two sheaves $j^{-1}F$ and $G$ are both $A_S(V\times_XS)$, by [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]; this gives the canonical identification in the statement. The same direct-image formula shows that $F|_{U_1}=0$, since $U_1\times_PS=\varnothing$. In particular its inverse image at infinity is zero, since infinity lies in $U_1$. Apply the module-sheaf version of [lem-weil-pbc-open-closed-short-exact] to $j:X\hookrightarrow P$ and its closed complement infinity, with coefficient sheaf $F$. Its last term is zero, so its first map $\epsilon_F:j_!j^{-1}F\to F$ is an isomorphism. Under $j^{-1}F=G$ this map is exactly $e$, not an arbitrary support isomorphism.

Use [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction] for the actual sheaf adjunction $j_!\dashv j^{-1}$. Both functors are additive and exact, by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact] and [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. Its localization to derived categories is the specified exact derived adjunction of [def-weil-exact-derived-adjunction]. In particular its derived counit is the localized original counit on sheaves and is a natural transformation on the whole ordinary derived category, including morphisms to shifted sheaves. We use this normalization for every $\epsilon_M$ below.

proof.text:
The pullback clause of [lem-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer], applied to $j$ and the Cartier pair of Step 1, identifies $j^{-1}c_{0,P}$ with $c_{0,X}$. The target identification $j^{-1}L_P[2]=L_X[2]$ is the roots- and tensor-normalized comparison of [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]; the source is the restriction identification of Step 2. Naturality of the counit of Step 3 at the actual arrow $c_{0,P}:F\to L_P[2]$ reads
$$c_{0,P}\circ\epsilon_F=\epsilon_{L_P[2]}\circ j_!j^{-1}(c_{0,P}).$$
Substituting these identifications gives exactly $c_{0,P}\circ e=\epsilon_{L_P[2]}\circ j_!c_{0,X}$. This uses no equality deduced merely from equality of restrictions of derived morphisms.

proof.text:
We check the source generator of the compact image. The closed immersion $\bar i_0$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-finite]. On abelian sheaves its direct image is exact by [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-direct-image-exact]; the derived direct-image composition of [def-weil-pbc-derived-direct-image-composition], for $S\xrightarrow{\bar i_0}P\to S$ whose composite is the identity, gives $H^q(P,F)=H^q(S,A_S)$. Here the equality is first for underlying abelian sheaves, then for module cohomology by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-module-cohomology-forget]. By [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-point-cohomology], these groups vanish for $q>0$ and are $A$ in degree zero, with identification given by sections on $S$. There is no negative cohomology for a sheaf in degree zero under right derived sections. Thus $R\Gamma(P,F)=A[0]$, normalized by the section $1$. By the chosen compactification definition [def-amb-etale-compact-support], $R\Gamma_c(X,G)=R\Gamma(P,j_!G)$; $R\Gamma(e)$ gives its canonical identification with $A[0]$. Let $\lambda:A\to R\Gamma(P,j_!G)$ be its inverse and $\eta:A\to R\Gamma(P,A_P)$ the constant-section map. If $u:A_P\to F$ is the closed unit, then
$$R\Gamma(e)\lambda=R\Gamma(u)\eta.$$
Indeed both sides are maps $A[0]\to A[0]$ sending $1$ to $1$: the formula for direct image and its unit sends the constant section $1$ to its restriction on $D_0=S$. An $A$-linear map $A\to A$ is determined by this value.

proof.text:
Apply derived global sections to the equality of Step 4 and precompose with $\lambda$ of Step 5. By [def-amb-etale-compact-support], $R\Gamma(j_!c_{0,X})\lambda=\tau_X^e$ and $R\Gamma(\epsilon_{L_P[2]})=a$. Step 5 therefore gives
$$a\tau_X^e=R\Gamma(c_{0,P})R\Gamma(e)\lambda=R\Gamma(c_{0,P}u)\eta.$$
The forgetting-support clause of [lem-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer] says $c_{0,P}u=c_1(\mathcal O_P(D_0))$. By the explicit line-bundle isomorphism of Step 1 this is $c_1(\mathcal O_P(1))$ with the positive Kummer boundary convention in the statement. Hence the last displayed morphism is the specified $h$. No generator was rescaled: the equality is with this Chern class itself, so its coefficient is $+1$.
